title: I made a Base Defense / Tower Defense game and I’d love for you to play it! =D
author: Pure_Requirement4469
selftext:
Hello, friends! I’m a 35-year-old Brazilian lawyer who loves strategy and base-defense games. For a few months now I’ve been thinking about and building a caravan-defense game, which will grow into a game of siege defense, fortress assaults, and even some RTS elements.

[https://luispaulotonini.itch.io/roads-and-fortresses](https://luispaulotonini.itch.io/roads-and-fortresses)

If the game doesn’t open, please let me know. I’m still learning how to use Itch.io. The game should work on PC or mobile.

For now, we have the sketch of a caravan-defense game, inspired by the Lusitanian regions and, later in the game, by Persian regions. I already have other regions ready to add to the game in the future.

I’d love for some friends to play it and give me feedback, report bugs, offer criticism, and suggest improvements.

So you’re already in the loop: the gold we’re earning in the game will be used in the future to rebuild the castle from the start of the game — which was taken and destroyed — and to kick off the siege-defense stages. Right now, gold is piling up and doesn’t have much use. Fame and other resources will have their uses improved. The cities you visit in the game will also come under siege in the future — at least that’s the idea. The images and items in the Book still have low graphic quality; I haven’t had time to improve them yet.

I know you’ll ask, so let me explain upfront. I didn’t use any magic trick or follow a specific workflow. The truth is I spent about 6 months playing around and exploring what the ChatGPT and Claude models can do. This particular game took about 60 days to reach its current state, across many sessions and different requests in Claude — a real mess of prompts, requests, and different sessions! =D

This whole project was built in Claude itself; ChatGPT only made a mess. I used Claude on Opus 5.5, a bit of Fable 5.2 in the last few days, and Suno for the music. I was building it in Unity with store assets, but that’s very laborious and slow, so I chose to migrate to Three.js version r187. Yes, the game is made almost entirely with several different AIs.

I’d really appreciate it if some of you could play it and give me ideas and feedback, especially whether you liked it and whether it’s fun, which is the main goal.

If you have questions about the project or how I’ve built it so far, I’ll be happy to answer.

A hug to all!

[https://luispaulotonini.itch.io/roads-and-fortresses](https://luispaulotonini.itch.io/roads-and-fortresses)

comments.author: RINgames
comments.body:
Great style and fun concept. I played through one map.

My feedback:

* The number one thing from me is that it needs to give me a reason to actually engage with the game. In part this looks like increasing the difficulty. Halfway through I realised that the things I was doing with my hero weren't necessary, and I just let go of the mouse and watched an 8 minute cutscene, and still made it to the castle just fine. But as well as difficulty, what I'd like to see most here is meaningful decisions. Even if you made every enemy deal more damage such that I needed to place my hero correctly or I'd lose, the core gameplay loop still lasts about three seconds and almost never changes. When it does change, the new gameplay elements also seem like they leave me little I need to be thinking about. I'd like to have a reason to be thinking along the way, a reason to choose between multiple different ways that I could approach the game that the outcome I get depends on.
* Similarly, the upgrades don't feel like they have any meaning to them. I ended up getting arrow upgrades and then escort sword upgrades, and then hero sword upgrades, but it felt like I could have picked randomly and had the same outcome. One thing you could do is add in upgrades that combo with one another: an elemental upgrade that slows bow shots but multiplies their damage, another that causes a fixed bonus damage per shot and so rewards faster shooting, and different upgrades for each of bow speed and bow damage, are together one example of how you could set something like that up.
* The book has way too much going on. My eyes glaze over when I open it. A primary reason for this is the low difficulty: there's absolutely no reason to read any of those pages full of text if none of it matters anyway. Adding in some reasons why your decisions matter, and then curating the info on those book pages so that it contains a high density of stuff that actually informs those decisions, would give the book a lot more value.
* I could not for the life of me work out how to earn gold. I kept passing shops that asked for gold, but I wasn't earning any and stayed at zero gold the whole time. Then when I finished the first level it showed me that I needed fame for hero upgrades, but I also hadn't earned any fame. Nothing indicated to me how to earn either of these.

I like the concept and I'd play it again if it gave me a reason to, but that core stuff needs some work at the moment.

replies.author: le_one_
replies.body: Spot on! I felt the same through my first playthrough. The game concept is great, but needs balancing.

replies.author: Pure_Requirement4469
replies.body:
Bom dia! Obrigado por responder! Eram justamente esses pontos que eu queria ajuda! 

Essa primeira estrada era para ser o tutorial, ela não dá ouro nem fama - que só começam a vir nas estradas seguintes. Pensei em fazer um tutorial onde o jogador "sempre vence", mesmo não sabendo jogar, para que ele conhecesse o jogo antes do jogo ficar mais difícil de verdade. Pelo visto ficou chato de jogar pois estava muito fácil!

Se você tiver paciência para jogar as outras estradas verá a questão do ouro e fama funcionando, e também a dificuldade vai aumentar bastante. Mas vou fazer as atualizações e daqui há alguns dias volto com uma boa atualização nos pontos que todos falam!

Muito obrigado pelo retorno meu amigo! Abraços!
